subject: Portfolio promo allocation + staged conversion to reserved capacity
messages:
From: Samantha Reed <samantha@venturecollective.org>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: split promo credits across portfolio + convert remainder to reserved discount

Hi Naomi / Ben,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Venture Collective has $75,000 in promo credits you provided for our Fall cohort. We'd like to do two things and want to understand Redwood's preferred path and accounting/ops implications:

1) Spread a portion of the credits across 12 portfolio companies (we suggest an initial allocation sheet attached). Some of those companies will be experimental and will not use all of their allocation in the first 90 days.

2) For credits that go unused after 90 days, we'd like to convert them into a committed Reserved/Dedicated discount for one portfolio company that is moving into production and will need sustained capacity. The company (BrightGrid) is ready to move to Dedicated but cannot commit to a full annual spend today; they'd prefer a staged reserved conversion for 3–6 months.

Questions:
- Can promo credits be split across accounts and then partially converted to reserved commit credit?
- If conversion is possible, what is the conversion mechanism (invoice/PO, prepay, commitment term) and recommended conversion ratio?
- Any tax / rev-rec considerations we should plan for on our side (we're non-profit aligned, but our SPVs are standard)?

I've attached a draft allocation sheet for visibility (VC_cohort_credit_schedule.xlsx). Can you let us know a proposed ops path and the steps (SOW, PO, DocuSign) so we can coordinate with BrightGrid's finance?

Appreciate the quick guidance — we have a board update next week and want to surface the path.

Cheers,
Samantha Reed
Director, Partnerships
Venture Collective
attachments: VC_cohort_credit_schedule.xlsx

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha@venturecollective.org>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: split promo credits across portfolio + convert remainder to reserved discount

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the clear ask and the allocation sheet. Short answer: yes, we can support both splitting promo credits across multiple accounts and converting unused credits into a reserved/dedicated credit, but there are a couple of standard controls we'll need to put in place (conversion window, per-account caps, and a short-term commitment for reserved capacity).

At a high level I propose the following so you have something to show the board:
- Initial split: allocate up to 60% of the promo pool across the 12 portfolio companies as direct usage credits (we can map each company's billing sub-account).
- Holdback: we place a 90-day holdback on the remaining 40% for potential conversion.
- Conversion option: unused holdback credits can be converted into a Reserved/Dedicated credit pool for a single company (BrightGrid). The conversion would require a signed SOW + purchase order from BrightGrid and a minimum 3-month reserved commit.

Ben will follow up with a conversion formula and a proforma so you can see the numbers. For tax/rev-rec we'll loop finance; generally credits converted to prepaid or committed discounts are treated differently than one-off promotional usage (we will provide written guidance).

I'll mark this as high priority and loop Irene from billing to confirm operational steps.

Best,
Naomi
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha@venturecollective.org>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: split promo credits across portfolio + convert remainder to reserved discount

Samantha — thanks for the context. Per Naomi's note, here's a practical set of options and the conversion mechanics so you can model outcomes. I've attached a short proposal and a proforma estimate (redwood_proposal_VC_v1.pdf, proforma_invoice_estimate.xlsx).

Option A – Full split (no conversion):
- Allocate credits: $45,000 (60%) allocated across 12 companies per your sheet. Each company gets a usage credit applied to their Redwood account. Unused credits expire after 90 days. No further obligations.

Option B – Split + staged conversion (recommended):
- Allocate credits: $40,000 split across cohort accounts (mapped to billing sub-accounts).
- Holdback: $35,000 remains in a conversion pool.
- Conversion trigger: After a 90-day evaluation window, VC confirms the amount to convert (min conversion $10k).
- Conversion mechanics: Converted credits are invoiced as a pre-paid credit toward Dedicated capacity. We create a short-term reserved commitment (3 months minimum) that draws down against a prepayment invoice. Conversion ratio proposal: 1 promo credit converts to $0.90 of pre-paid reserved credit value (reflects discount + administrative handling). Example: $10,000 promo => $9,000 pre-paid reserved credit applied to Dedicated pool.
- Billing ops: Requires SOW from BrightGrid, PO or company acceptance, and DocuSign on a short amendment. We will record the prepayment as deferred revenue on Redwood's books; we will provide standard language for VC's finance team.

Important notes:
- Per-company usage caps: we can enforce soft-limits to prevent one early adopter from consuming the whole split allocation.
- Refunds: Converted prepayments are non-refundable but may be transferable within VC's portfolio with prior agreement.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm preferred allocation numbers (which cohort companies and amounts).
2) If you want Option B, confirm the conversion floor ($10k) and which company will be the conversion candidate (BrightGrid).
3) We'll issue the proforma invoice and the DocuSign amendment for BrightGrid; Irene will handle the PO/invoice mapping.

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_proposal_VC_v1.pdf; proforma_invoice_estimate.xlsx

From: Mike Liao <mike@venturecollective.org>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Samantha Reed <samantha@venturecollective.org>
Date: 2026-09-15T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: split promo credits across portfolio + convert remainder to reserved discount

Thanks Ben — a couple quick questions from BrightGrid's finance side before we sign anything: 
1) How will the invoice line item look if we convert $10k in credits? Will it say "Prepaid reserved capacity – applied credit"? We need the description for our GL mapping.
2) On the conversion ratio (1 -> 0.90), can you include a worked example for 3-, 6-, and 12-month reserved terms? BrightGrid is evaluating whether a 6-month staged commit makes sense.
3) Any compliance/security evidence we need to show to BrightGrid before they move to Dedicated (they asked for SOC2 score and data residency confirmation)?

If you've got a one-page that answers 1–3 we can get PO approval quickly.

Best,
Mike Liao
CFO, BrightGrid (on behalf of Venture Collective)

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mike Liao <mike@venturecollective.org>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-16T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: split promo credits across portfolio + convert remainder to reserved discount

Hi Mike — looping in billing/ops capacity. Quick answers and next steps: 

1) Invoice language: We will generate a prepayment invoice with the description: "Prepaid Dedicated capacity credit (converted from promotional credit) – applied to account: BrightGrid". Our finance team will include the HubSpot deal id in the invoice memo for GL mapping.

2) Worked examples (conversion at 0.90 factor):
- $10,000 promo -> $9,000 pre-paid credit; 3-month reserved (monthly draw): $3,000/month credit applied to Dedicated usage.
- $10,000 promo -> $9,000 pre-paid credit; 6-month reserved: $1,500/month credit.
- $10,000 promo -> $9,000 pre-paid credit; 12-month reserved: $750/month credit.

If BrightGrid prefers a stepped commitment (3 months then option to renew to 6), we can structure the SOW to reflect a 3-month minimum with an automatic renewal clause unless they provide 30-day notice.

3) Compliance pack: please find our security summary link and SOC 2 evidence request process here: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-evidence. We typically provide a SOC2 attestation copy and a data residency confirmation letter by request; I'll attach the standard security stub to the DocuSign packet.

Operational checklist to proceed: 
- VC confirms allocation table and conversion floor (reply-all).
- BrightGrid to sign the DocuSign amendment (link: https://docusign.com/links/abcdef1234567890).
- BrightGrid issues PO referencing invoice number once proforma is approved.
- Billing issues final invoice and applies prepayment credit on activation.

Cc'ing Accounting (internal) — we'll prepare the proforma when you confirm Option B. Our HubSpot record is HUBSPOT-VC-9083.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Billing & Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
attachments: security-SOC2-evidence-request-stub.pdf
